findings.summary: The log audit does not check the stop that B14 reads. realism takes the stop from the request log's end record, start_unix + end_mono (scripts/traffic_log.py:869-870). summarize checks only the interval log's end record against its last interval (traffic_log.py:617-618). Nothing compares the request log's end_mono with the interval log's, with the post marker or with the last request. Nothing ties the arrivals' t_utc, which the rule compares with the stop, to start_unix + t_mono. The message of commit 89129e4 says 'The log audit ties end_mono to the log: summarize compares the interval log's copy of the same record with the last interval'. That is true only of the interval log's copy. The two copies agree only because host_traffic.py Writer.finish writes one dict to both logs. A moved stop is accepted and leaves out the wrong user sessions. A stop moved later, or before the origin, brings back B13's stop-biased low share. A stop moved into the measure phase leaves out other sessions and keeps the cut buyers. A stop at the last arrival leaves no share, and the session is refused. The error leans toward refusal. The exception is a share that is really too high, which a later stop could pull back into tolerance. Honest logs are not affected.

findings.suggested_fix: Compare the stop in the generator's monotonic time, each arrival's t_mono against end_mono, so start_unix no longer matters. Also refuse a /2 pair whose request-log end_mono differs from the interval log's, for example with a problem requests:end_mono_mismatch in summarize. The alternative is to read the interval log's end_mono, which intervals_not_to_end already binds. Add a self-test case that moves only the request log's end_mono. This is measurement code, so it reopens G0. It can go with the next change that reopens G0, before traffic_realism is judged on G2 or G3 sessions. Until then the G0 record can name the gap, and the claim in 89129e4's message should not be repeated.
